conversation: Good to see everyone. My family taught me to fish here, and I want this lake to keep supporting our village. With 100 tons in the lake, we can catch 50 tons total and leave 50 to double back to 100 next month. How about we each take 10 tons this month? That’s $10,000 apiece, and we can keep earning that every month if we stick to the limit. Let’s check our catches together afterward and agree on next month’s plan. John, does that sound fair to you?

I’m on board, Luke—I’ll keep my catch to 10 tons. My family depended on this lake, and I want the village’s children to have that same livelihood. Let’s make sure all five of us agree before heading out, and if the stock ever falls below 100 tons, adjust our limits together. John, are you willing to commit to 10 tons too?

Count me in for 10 tons. I learned to fish here from my family, and a steady living matters more than one big haul that leaves the village short later. Let’s record our catches together each month so everyone can see we’re keeping our word. John and Jack, can you both commit to the same limit?

I’ll commit to 10 tons too. My family taught me to leave enough fish for the next season, and this plan gives us a steady income without draining the lake. If anyone needs extra income one month, let’s talk before fishing rather than quietly exceeding the limit. Jack, will you join us at 10 tons?

I’m in—I’ll take no more than 10 tons. That gives all five of us a fair living while leaving enough fish to replenish the lake. Let’s meet after this month’s catches are recorded and check that we’re on track. See you out there.
